Dave Checketts, veteran sports executive and investor, joins Portfolio Players for a conversation on ownership, expansion, and the evolving economics of global sports.

Checketts breaks down:
 • Why scarcity is the single biggest driver of franchise value
 • The investment strategy behind his fund and why cash flow matters
 • Michael Jordan/Knicks stories, lessons from Utah & New York 
 • The realities of launching new leagues and why venture capital often stays away
 • His perspective on MLS growth, global soccer, and media rights
 • The rise of NIL and why education still needs to be prioritized

column10: From Olympic Gold to Founder: Allyson Felix’s Next Chapter
column11:
Allyson Felix, 7-time Olympics gold medalist turned investor, joins Portfolio Players for a conversation on the future of women’s sports, athlete-led investing, and the evolving business of track and field.

Felix breaks down:
 • Her role shaping the vision for the LA28 Summer Olympics
 • Why track and field is at a pivotal moment globally
 • How athlete investors are becoming a more influential voice in sports
 • The strategy behind Always Alpha and backing women’s sports founders
 • Building Saysh and creating products designed for female athletes
 • The evolving ownership landscape and where she would invest next
 • Why representation at the decision-making level matters more than ever
 • What it takes to build lasting impact beyond competition

This episode of Portfolio Players, presented by E*TRADE from Morgan Stanley, explores how athlete founders, capital, and long-term vision are reshaping the future of sports.

Is perfect officiating via AI actually bad for sports? Premier Lacrosse League cofounder and President Paul Rabil thinks so.

He pointed to the FA Cup deliberately keeping VAR out. Not despite the missed calls, but because of them.

column10:
Jerry Jones bought the Dallas Cowboys for $140 million in 1989.

The franchise is now worth $11 billion.

That's not an outlier — it's the pattern. Cofounder and President of the Premier Lacrosse League Paul Rabil breaks down why sports ownership has compounded at \~15% annually over the last 35 years, putting it at 50-100x total returns versus the stock market's 15x over the same period.

The math is why institutional capital is rotating into sports. It's not passion money anymore — it's patient capital chasing the best risk-adjusted return in alternatives.

column10: Paul Rabil: Why Owning a Team Is a 100x Bet
column11:
Premier Lacrosse League cofounder and former superstar Paul Rabil joins Portfolio Players for a conversation on disrupting pro sports, building a league from scratch, and why team ownership has become one of the most coveted assets in investing.

Rabil breaks down:
 • Why owning a sports team can generate 50–100x returns
 • How the PLL became the first lacrosse league to sell distribution rights to major networks
 • The touring model that differentiated PLL from legacy leagues
 • Why former athletes make natural team owners
 • How private equity reshaped sports ownership
 • Why sports is “AI proof” in a tech-driven world
 • Whether fans actually enjoy ads during live games
 • The challenge of growing lacrosse nationally
 • Why short-format leagues can be difficult for sponsors
 • The key difference between sports and business

This episode of Portfolio Players, presented by E*TRADE from Morgan Stanley, explores how capital, media strategy, and athlete-led innovation are reshaping the future of professional sports leagues.

 • Why every league must start with what matters most to fans

 • What it looks like to partner with athletes instead of merely employing them
 • Why the “G League model” doesn’t work for independent properties
 • How athlete personal branding drives league growth

 • The path to profitable operations in emerging markets
